focus: Select/archive/restore/delete identity transitions; active and last-unarchived project protection; rejection preserves state.

inspected.inspection: ProjectLibrary value-state and identity mutation methods, especially lines 91–134; file-store implementation excluded
Identity-related tests at lines 12–33, 96–131 and 147–198; remaining test declarations scanned

checks.result: select first resolves the ID, rejects an archived record, and only then changes activeID. Existing scenes and records remain untouched; failed lookup or archive guard does not mutate state.

archive rejects activeID before changing an archive flag. For a valid snapshot this also protects the last unarchived project. Archiving an inactive record retains activeID and all record identities/content; missing ID throws before assignment.
restore changes only the located record's archive flag. It neither replaces the UUID nor selects the restored record. Unknown IDs throw before mutation. Repeated restore is an idempotent assignment.
Repeated archive of an inactive archived record and repeated restore of an unarchived record do not change any other state. A restore of the current unarchived active record is a no-op.

deleteArchived resolves the ID, requires a different ID from activeID and an archived flag, then removes exactly that index. The active and unrelated records are preserved, preventing deletion of the last active project in a valid snapshot.

All possible errors in the scoped methods occur before their single mutation. Existing tests compare the full library after invalid selection and rejected live/active/missing deletion. The archive/restore round-trip checks active identity and scene preservation.

checks.result: All inspected files were fetched with the requested full commit SHA. Commit metadata confirms the revision and its retained historical evidence commit message.

coverage_notes: The scoped test file does not separately assert every missing-ID archive/restore rejection, exact archive error type, or the singleton last-active case. Source ordering and guards cover these cases; this observation is not a demonstrated product defect.
